paper_metadata.title: White Matter Microstructural Alterations over the Year after Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients with Baseline Impaired Cognitive Functions

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a consecutive recruitment strategy with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria. The target population (AIS patients with baseline cognitive impairment) is well-described, and the use of a matched healthy control group strengthens the representativeness.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Sixty patients showing impaired cognitive functions within 3 days after AIS (baseline) and 25 healthy controls underwent diffusion kurtosis imaging scan and cognitive assessment at baseline and 1 year.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the clinical condition (AIS), the timing (within 3 days), and the cognitive status (impaired) required for the source population.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: A consecutive study was approved by the Medical Research Ethics Committee and conducted at the corresponding hospital between 2018 and 2020.
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment is the gold standard for limiting selection bias in prognosis studies.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: conducted at the corresponding hospital between 2018 and 2020.
items.reasoning: The specific years of recruitment are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Department of Radiology, Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing 100020, China
items.reasoning: The specific hospital and city are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The inclusion criteria included: (1) diagnosis of the first AIS, clinical assessment, and MRI within 3 days after stroke onset; (2) National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score at admission between 1 and 15...
items.reasoning: Detailed criteria including NIHSS scores, education levels, and specific MRI scores (MTA) are provided.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Eighty-five participants were enrolled after excluding poor imaging quality and incomplete clinical information.
items.reasoning: While the final number is clear, the total number of eligible patients screened versus those who declined to participate is not reported, making it difficult to calculate a participation rate.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Baseline characteristics and clinical data of participants are presented in Table 1.
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive list of demographics, vascular risk factors, and cognitive scores.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports on 60 patients at both baseline and 1 year, implying a 100% follow-up rate for the enrolled cohort. However, the exclusion of participants due to 'poor imaging quality' or 'incomplete clinical information' occurred at the enrollment phase, and there is no mention of dropouts during the 1-year interval, which is unusual for a stroke cohort.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: All 60 original patients... 25 were diagnosed as PSCI and 35 recovered to normal cognition
items.reasoning: The text suggests all 60 patients who met the final enrollment criteria completed the 1-year follow-up.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (KFA and MK) are measured using advanced, objective MRI techniques (DKI) with standardized processing (FSL, TBSS). The use of a 3.0T scanner and blinded evaluation of other radiological markers further reduces bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: DKE software was applied to calculate the FA, KFA, and MK. The TBSS method was performed on the previous parameters for statistical analysis.
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors (KFA/MK) are clearly defined within the context of Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: MRI data were acquired using the same 3.0 T brain MRI (Achieva; Philips Healthcare, Best, Netherlands).
items.reasoning: The use of high-field MRI and established software (FSL/DKE) ensures high reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: The FA-threshold for the skeleton was >0.2 to include all major WM tracts
items.reasoning: The study uses standard, non-data-dependent thresholds for TBSS analysis.

items.evidence_snippet: Patients and the HC group were scanned once at admission and again at 1 year. MRI data were acquired using the same 3.0 T brain MRI
items.reasoning: All participants underwent the same imaging protocol on the same equipment.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (PSCI) is defined using validated clinical scales (MMSE, MoCA) administered by experienced neurologists. The 1-year follow-up is an appropriate timeframe for assessing chronic cognitive status post-stroke.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: PSCI was diagnosed according to the cognitive performance 1 year after stroke... MoCA score <26 indicated CI.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined by specific scores at a specific time point (1 year).

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: neuropsychological assessments at baseline and 1 year by two experienced neurologists... including the mini-mental state examination (MMSE) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA).
items.reasoning: MMSE and MoCA are validated tools, and assessment by two experienced clinicians increases reliability.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All participants in the AIS and HC groups underwent two neuropsychological assessments at baseline and 1 year
items.reasoning: The protocol was identical for both patients and controls.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for several key confounders (age, education, NIHSS) in the statistical models. However, while it mentions 'strategic brain region infarct' as an independent risk factor, it is unclear if the primary DKI analysis (TBSS) was fully adjusted for the specific location of the acute infarct in every voxel-wise comparison.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is robust, using FWE correction for multiple comparisons in the imaging analysis and appropriate longitudinal models (Two-way repeated measures ANOVA). The results are presented transparently with MNI coordinates and voxel counts.

items.evidence_snippet: Skeletonized DKI maps obtained from the TBSS approach were analyzed using the general linear model... Randomized function in FSL was used for voxel-wise statistical tests.
items.reasoning: The analytical steps for both clinical and imaging data are well-documented.
